name: a worn stone seat
description: A seat cut from a single block of red stone, the arms polished to a shine by hands, the front edge worn into a shallow dip by generations of the backs of knees.
looks: The dip in the seat is exactly the shape of somebody. It is not exactly your shape, and that bothers you more than it should.
There are marks cut into the underside of the arm where nobody would ever see them. They are a tally, and it is a long one.
It is warm. There is no sun in here and it is warm.
says: Others have sat. It held them.
You may. It is not a throne. It is only very old.
The count under the arm is not people. Do not worry about the count.
emotes: {it} takes the light along one polished arm as if somebody just ran a hand down it.
Dust settles on {it} and, a moment later, is not on it any more.
{it} sits in the middle of the floor as though the room was built around it, which it now appears to have been.
asks: Are you going to sit, or are you working out whether you are allowed?
Who told you about this room?
Do you know how many that tally is up to?
